the Rabbanan disputing R' Yehuda on the tally
the Gemara's own voice: דלא כרבי יהודה, במאי קא מיפלגי, the מאי טעמא questions and answers, כמאן, פשיטא, ואימא הכי נמי

props.gloss_en: the mishnah: one sounds no fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple, and no more than forty-eight
the mishnah is not in accordance with R' Yehuda
R' Yehuda: one who minimises shall not go below seven; one who adds shall not go above sixteen
R' Yehuda holds: tekia, terua, tekia is one [blast]
the Rabbanan hold: a tekia is [counted] by itself and a terua by itself
R' Yehuda's reason: the verse says 'and you shall sound (utkatem) a terua', and it is written 'a terua they shall sound (yitke'u)' -- how so? tekia and terua are one
the Rabbanan: that [verse] comes for a plain blast before it and after it
and R' Yehuda -- before it and after it, from where? he derives it from 'a second time' (shenit)
the Rabbanan's reason: it is written 'and when assembling the congregation you shall sound a tekia and not a terua'
R' Yehuda: that [tekia at the assembly] comes merely as a signal
the Rabbanan: it is a signal, and the Merciful One made it a mitzva
Rav Kahana: between tekia and terua there is nothing at all
whose view does Rav Kahana's dictum follow? R' Yehuda's
R' Yochanan: one who heard nine blasts at nine hours of the day has fulfilled [his obligation]

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יהודה, לפניה ולאחריה מנליה? -- the Rabbanan read his verse as the source of the plain blasts around the terua; if he spends it on 'one blast', from where does he get them?
ורבנן מאי טעמייהו? ובהקהיל את הקהל תתקעו ולא תריעו -- ואי סלקא דעתך תקיעה תרועה אחת היא, אמר רחמנא פלגא דמצוה עביד ופלגא לא עביד?! (the stam giving the Rabbanan's reason)

answered_by.gloss_en: ורבי יהודה: ההוא לסימנא בעלמא הוא דאתא (= p_behakhil_lesimana). The Rabbanan's rejoinder at 53b.13 -- סימנא הוא ורחמנא שוייה מצוה (p_simana_veshavyeh_mitzva) -- attacks this answer; the schema cannot attack an answer (header)

objections.gloss_en: ואימא הכי נמי! -- say indeed that Rav Kahana holds even like the Rabbanan, and comes only to exclude R' Yochanan's nine hours

answered_by.gloss_en: אם כן, מאי ״ולא כלום״? -- 'nothing at all' admits no pause whatever, which fits only R' Yehuda's one blast
